note:
Seeded 2026-08-16 with the lane itself.

Service-worker scope was never checked against the right globals: lib.dom and
lib.webworker cannot share a program, so `ServiceWorkerGlobalScope`, `Clients`,
`ExtendableEvent`, `PushEvent` and the rest simply do not exist in the program
the other three lanes compile. What they reported for these files was measured
against `Window`.

The number is the SUM of three programs, because a TS program is one global
scope and each deployed worker is its own:

    /web/service-worker.js     web + mail, concatenated by mail/controllers/webmanifest.py   51
    /pos/service-worker.js     point_of_sale/controllers/main.py                              3
    /event/service-worker.js   website_event_track/controllers/webmanifest.py                33

Summed rather than floored three ways so that moving a file between routes does
not read as drift; what this gate is for is that the scope stops growing.

Both strictness flags are on, unlike the two DOM lanes which carry one each.
Those are split because each ratchets its own history over `web`; this scope has
no history to ratchet, so it starts at the full bar.

87 is what the scope measures once it is compiled correctly, NOT what it
measured before: the same four files reported 119 under the DOM lanes, and that
reading was wrong in both directions -- it missed every real service-worker
error and invented `self` errors that only existed because `self` was typed
`Window`. The two numbers are not comparable and neither is an improvement on
the other.

Of the 87, the residual after the lane itself is ordinary annotation work:
IndexedDB handlers reading `event.target.result` off `EventTarget`, `{Object}`
parameters, implicitly-any accumulators. None of it needed the lane; all of it
was invisible without it.
